answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a karst, before it can post or attest. A single terrace checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 357 aliases therefore costs 231 bonds held for 6 days each, plus the hollow attestations those aliases can never earn. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
